data.title: Zelenskyy says Starlink restored to full speed
data.description:
• Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday said that the military-grade version of SpaceX's (SPCX) Starlink satellite network in Ukraine considered critical in its ongoing war with Russia has been restored to full speed.
  • "The most important thing today is that Starlink and Starshield operations have been restored to the speeds we had before the restrictions," he wrote on X. "The speeds are now where they need to be."
  • Ukrainian drones that rely on Starlink's Starshield satellite network are now operating at 250 miles per hour (ca. 402 km/h), the same as before speeds were slowed earlier this month, The New York Times reported.
  • On Oct. 14, the Ukrainian military reported that Starlink speeds were throttled, negatively impacting their operations.
  • President Trump last week reportedly asked Elon Musk to restore Starlink speeds in Ukraine after the SpaceX CEO allegedly limited them.

data.title: Consumer Discretionary Earnings: EPS beats outpace revenue
data.description:
Consumer discretionary companies delivered stronger results against EPS expectations than revenue estimates this week.

Six of nine beat on earnings, but only four topped revenue forecasts. Year-over-year revenue increased at five companies, compared with four that grew EPS.

Here’s a look at how the companies performed:

  • General Motors (GM): adj. EPS of $3.70 beats by $0.07; Revenue of $50.02B (+2.9% Y/Y) beats by $1.26B
  • Genuine Parts Company (GPC): adj. EPS of $2.07 beats by $0.03; Revenue of $6.52B (+4.2% Y/Y) beats by $30M
  • Hasbro (HAS): adj. EPS of $2.90 beats by $1.05; Revenue of $1.60B beats by $120M.
  • Tesla (TSLA): adj. EPS of $0.48 beats by $0.03; Revenue of $28.05B (-0.1% Y/Y) misses by $200M.
  • Las Vegas Sands (LVS): adj. EPS of $0.54 misses by $0.14; Revenue of $3.22B (-3.3% Y/Y) misses by $110M.
  • Tractor Supply Company (TSCO): adj. EPS of $0.43 beats by $0.02; Revenue of $3.91B (+5.1% Y/Y) beats by $90M.
  • PulteGroup (PHM): EPS of $2.53 misses by $0.09; Revenue of $3.98B (-9.5% Y/Y) misses by $170M.
  • Deckers Outdoor (DECK): EPS of $2.31 beats by $0.52; Revenue of $1.48B (+3.5% Y/Y) misses by $30M.
  • NVR (NVR): EPS of $89.45 misses by $11.88.; Revenue of $2.35B (-8.0% Y/Y) misses by $100M.

Next week, Amazon (AMZN) is expected to report EPS of $1.96 on revenue of $202.20B. Ford (F) is forecast to earn $0.40 per share on revenue of $45.81B, while Starbucks (SBUX) is expected to post EPS of $0.71 on revenue of $9.24B. Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG) is projected to report EPS of $0.29 on revenue of $3.29B.

Consumer Discretionary ETFs: (XLY), (VCR), (FXD), (FDIS), (RSPD), and (RXI).

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Intel, Apple and Zoom among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, after investors digested corporate results from big companies including Netflix and Meta Platforms during the week. However, technology stocks continued to lag amid artificial intelligence spending fears and a continued rise in oil prices due to geopolitical turmoil.

Wall Street analysts issued fresh round of upgrades and downgrades. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Intel’s AI computing demand could support earnings, says JPM

Intel (INTC) shares were upgraded at JPMorgan to Neutral from Underweight on improved execution under chief Lip-Bu Tan and growing demand for AI computing that could support earnings growth.

"Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading-edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27 (our CY28 EPS estimates are ~15% above consensus)," said analyst Harlan Sur.

Zoom Communications in focus on Outperform upgrade

Oppenheimer upgraded Zoom Communications (ZM) to Outperform from Perform with a $130 price target.

“We are upgrading ZM from Perform to Outperform with a $130 price target as we gain confidence in its transition from video meetings to a broader AI communications and workflow platform,” Oppenheimer analyst Timothy Horan wrote.

Delving deeper, Horan said the company's AI Platform has its own unique data, AI models and comes with “excellent security and governance.” It also combines meetings, productivity apps, unified communications and contact center, along with ZoomMate.

Apple downgraded on iPhone shipment concerns

Loop Capital downgraded Apple (AAPL) to Hold from Buy, citing concerns about a cut in iPhone shipments.

“The gist is that when AAPL previously reduced its Sep Q & Dec Q iPhone unit ships by 10% we believed they would be in a position to make up many (if not most) of these units through CY2027 as the reductions were supply related (memory & processors) & not demand related,” Loop Capital analyst Ananda Baruah wrote, adding that “this no longer appears to be the case.”

“We continue to like AAPL’s longer-term share gain and Services story… but believe the stock also requires a fundamental catalyst reset after its recent stock appreciation... particularly given its trading at 5-year valuation highs as iPhone ships have been reduced and [gross margin] could see incremental pressure,” the analyst added.

Alcoa downgraded on near-term challenges

Argus downgraded Alcoa (AA) to Hold from Buy, as aluminum prices remain near multi-month lows as supply improves outside the Middle East.

Alcoa is having trouble overcoming the pricing pressures, prompting Argus analyst Alexandra Yates to reduce her rating until seeing more of a rebound in the market driven by long-term sustainable demand.

Yates also said she is concerned about market volatility, as Alcoa is heavily exposed to the global market and faces potential downside from expanding supplies and investment in production capacity by competitors.

Seaport Research reiterated its Sell rating on Nvidia (NVDA), noting competition is “mounting.”

“We could be wrong about Nvidia in the coming months, as they leverage their supply chain heft, but competitive pressures are mounting,” Seaport analyst Jay Goldberg wrote. “We see their aggressive finance bundling as a reaction to competitive pressure and a strategic tension at the heart of their business.”

Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX) was double-upgraded to Buy from Sell by Phillip Securities as Super Intelligence swings the company into profit, according to a media report. Analyst Glenn Thum said he raised FY26 revenue by 56% to $45.1 billion and lifted FY27 by 201% to $132 billion on higher Super Intelligence revenue. The company's PT was more than tripled to $250 from $75.

Accenture (ACN) was downgraded to Neutral at Baird as the investment firm said the risk-reward on the stock is in balance after a near 100% increase since June. Despite the downgrade, the brokerage upped the price target on the stock to $252 from $245.

Akamai (AKAM) was upgraded by Raymond James to Strong Buy from Outperform, citing a revenue boost from its deal with Anthropic (ANTHRO).

data.title: 5 out of 5 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Netflix (NFLX) and Meta Platforms (META).

The communications services sector (XLC) lost over 8% so far this year, compared to the nearly 12% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, five tickers reported results, all of which reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, four companies exceeded revenue expectations, while one company trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Netflix (NFLX) shares closed 5% lower on Wednesday following a weaker-than-expected revenue outlook. The streaming giant reported third-quarter revenue of $12.9B, in line with Wall Street estimates, but forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $13.4B, below analysts’ expectations.

Similarly, Meta Platforms (META) slipped 7% after the company’s third-quarter results. Meta’s Q3 earnings showed an increase of 26% in revenues over the past year to a record high of $64.6B. However, its costs and expenses showed an increase of 68% year-over-year. The company now expects to spend $135B to $145B on capital expenditures, increasing the lower end from $130B but remaining within estimates of $138B in capex.

Investors were also disappointed after AT&T’s (T) postpaid phone subscriber additions for the third quarter came in below expectations. Even though the telecom company reported revenue and adjusted earnings above consensus estimates, shares still closed over 6% lower on Wednesday.

For the upcoming week, Alphabet (GOOG), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile US (TMUS) are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Eli Lilly releases promising early-stage data on ADC for ovarian cancer
data.description:
• Phase 1 data on Eli Lilly's (LLY) sofetabart mipitecan (Sofe-M) found that the antibody-drug conjugate plus Avastin (bevacizumab) led to high objective response and disease control rates in individuals with platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer.
  • Results showed that the combo led to a 79% confirmed objective response rate and 100% disease control rate. Similac reponses were seen across folate receptor alpha (FRα) expression levels.
  • Participants had a median of three prior systemic regimens.
  • The most common treatment-emergent adverse events were epistaxis, nausea, anemia, neutropenia, and fatigue. The most common Grade ≥3 TEAEs were neutropenia and anemia.
  • The FRAmework-01 program is examining the FRα antibody-drug conjugate in both platinum-resistant and platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer in three phase 3 trials: Part A as monotherapy in platinum-resistant disease; Part B tests Sofe-M plus Avastin in platinum-sensitive disease that progressed on or within six months of completing a PARP inhibitor (PARPi); and Part C examines Sofe-M plus Avastin in PARPi-naïve platinum-sensitive disease.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway, Blackstone in gainers; HSBC, Globe Life among losers: week's financials wrap
data.description:
Wall Street closed the week mixed as a sharp spike in volatility reflected fresh tech struggles, while investors continued to digest hotter-than-expected CPI data and the latest bank earnings.

State Street Financial Sel Sec SPDR ETF (XLF) advanced 0.68% from the previous week to close at $55.90.

Among megacap stocks, Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD) led the weekly gainers, adding 3.51% to close at $124.61.

The week saw the Canadian lender's U.S. unit launch TD Credit Assist, an AI capability that reduces the time required to prepare a first-draft commercial credit analysis from up to three working days to less than 30 minutes.

"By reducing time spent on manual preparation, our credit professionals can focus more of their time on understanding the client, assessing risk, and moving opportunities forward," said Jill Gateman, Head of Commercial Banking, TD Bank U.S.

Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) (BRK.B) followed with 1.95% and 1.91% gains to $813,595.00 and $542.19, respectively.

B shares touched a new high on Wednesday, an indication that investors have become more confident in Greg Abel, who succeeded Warren Buffett as CEO on Jan. 1, 2026.

HSBC Holdings (HSBC) was the top decliner, retreating 4.11% to $90.68.

The global lender is set to post its third-quarter financial results next week; and even as earnings are expected to come in strong on the back of higher interest rates and resilient Asian wealth management fees, mounting cost pressures and regulatory uncertainty from China may impact stock prices.

Japanese lender Mitsubishi UFJ (MUFG) (-3.70% W/W to $21.07) was the next on the list.

The week saw Japanese banks, along with other organizations, temporarily take digital services offline in response to certain security vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Separately, the Bank of Japan warned of rising risks from AI, including growing cybersecurity threats and potential ‌market shocks, that could impact the country's banking system.

Globe Life (GL) was among the top largecap losers, retreating 8.28% week-over-week to $154.79.

The life and health insurer was downgraded to Neutral from Overweight at Piper Sandler after reporting third-quarter earnings below Wall Street estimates this week.

First Citizens Bancshares (FCNCA) led the gainers, advancing 11.87% to $2,375.84. The stock was gaining after posting better-than-expected Q3 earnings and announcing a new $1.2B stock buyback program.

Blackstone (BX) added 10.66% from the prior week to $117.97 even as Q3 earnings fell short of consensus.

TransUnion (TRU) (+9.99% W/W to $81.48) extended gains from the previous week, when a general strength was seen across the broader credit reporting sector.

Among midcap stocks, UWM Holdings (UWMC) (+38.10% W/W to $1.45) was the top advancer. The mortgage finance provider reported its preliminary unaudited results for the quarter ended September 30, as part of which it said it expects to report total revenue between $800M and $825M, above the consensus of $651.35M.

FirstCash Holdings (FCFS) (-19.75% W/W to $172.75) was the top loser in the category despite a Q3 beat and dividend raise. 

Better Home & Finance (BETR) (+68.04% W/W to $16.72), Chaince Digital (CD) (+26.41% W/W to $8.76), Stewart Information Services (STC) (-16.12% W/W to $44.07), and Gemini Space Station (GEMI) (-14.29% W/W to $3.06) were the notable smallcap movers.

data.title: Revenge of the consumer: Walmart's $120 bundle takes on Amazon and Costco
data.description:
Walmart (WMT) unveiled a bundled Walmart+ and Sam’s Club Plus membership option this week in a direct challenge to Amazon Prime (AMZN) and Costco (COST). The joint membership costs $120 per year, which is a saving of $100 per year. It's also $19 cheaper than an annual Amazon Prime membership at $139 and $10 cheaper than Costco's $130 Executive membership but $55 more than Costco's $65 Gold Star membership. The biggest savings are for shoppers who now pay for both Prime and a Costco Executive membership, who would save $149 a year by switching to the bundle.

"This is a direct shot at Prime," United National Consumer Suppliers CEO Brett Rose told Retail Dive. He noted that at $120 per year a member gets a warehouse club, delivery, streaming, and gas thrown in. On paper, Walmart wins the value math easily, highlighted Rose.

“The timing tells you everything. Consumers are stretched heading into the holidays, and memberships lock in loyalty and recurring revenue before the spending gets decided,” Rose said. “Loyalty programs are what keep people coming back. However, not more so than lower prices.”

On Wall Street, Oppenheimer analyst Rupesh Parikh and his team believe consumers are the clear winners from the development due to the stronger combination of perks, the ability to have Walmart and Sam’s Club products delivered to your home with no markups, and minimal incremental costs to upgrade. "This new offering further strengthens Walmart's membership value proposition vs. Amazon Prime and COST. To the extent this membership program takes off, WMT should enjoy incremental wallet share gains, especially on the delivery front, but there is a likely initial P&L headwind near term," advised Parikh.

Looking ahead, the timing of the Walmart (WMT) just ahead of the holidays could put incremental pressure on Amazon (AMZN) and Costco (COST) to dial up promotional activity.

data.title: Iran in 'advanced stages' of plans to target US officials in Middle East
data.description:
• US intelligence has information that Iran is in the 'advanced stages' of plots targeting government officials in the Middle East and beyond, according to a memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.
  • "Specifically, through various channels, we have received intelligence that Iran has substantiallyincreased efforts to target U.S. personnel," Clayton's memo to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, dated Oct. 23 and obtained by Axios, reads. 
  • Clayton noted he will try to downgrade as much intelligence as he can so Rubio can share the information as widely as possible with personnel who may be impacted.
  • The memo comes following a report in The New York Times on Oct. 21 that the US and Israel have drawn up plans to resume strikes on Iran after the midterm elections. 
  • In late September, a Wall Street Journal report said that Trump told advisors he wants to resume bombing after the midterms.

data.title: Vibe Theft Auto: Anthropic Opus, GTA 6, and a potential fade trade
data.description:
The adoption of AI around the video game industry is accelerating, which is raising new opportunities for publishers on the development end, but also creating risks around AI-enabled game recompilation and decompilation. Anthropic's (ANTHRO) latest released Opus version sent a shockwave in the video game sector as it opened up investors to the concept that platform-locked games are portable and games can be easily decompiled.

Vibe coding, which is the practice of describing what you want to an AI model in plain language and letting it write, test, and fix the code, became a major topic after the release of Opus 5.5. That led to some video game stocks selling off amid increased concerns that AI agents can take a shipped game and reconstruct it, turning what was once years of volunteer reverse engineering into days or even hours. 

Digging into the development, Oppenheimer analyst Martin Yang pointed to more than 20 high-profile decompiling projects between mid-September and mid-October. In one case a fleet of AI agents rebuilt the 2009 shooter Modern Warfare 2 from its executable, reaching 99% of functions reconstructed. In other cases, new games saw free copycat versions pop up. "Given the rapid AI model release cadence from leading labs, we see rising AI-headline selloff risks in gaming," he warned.

However, where there is fear, there is also opportunity. Roblox (RBLX) was singled out as resistant to left-tail risks from AI and expected to be an AI benefiiciary.

Looking to the upcoming release of Take-Two Interactive's (TTWO) Grand Theft Auto 6, Yang pointed out that investors could fade any unwarranted, headline-driven share price sell-offs tied to a source code leak or jailbroken version of the highly anticipated game.

Yang highlighted that in a sea of AI slop games, Take-Two Interactive's (TTWO) games will always stand out for their attention to detail and crafted storytelling. "The server-dependent experiences such as GTA Online are less directly exposed to executable copying," he added. 

Related video game ETFs include the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO), the Global X Video Games & Esports ETF (HERO), the Amplify Video Game Leaders ETF (GAMR), and the Roundhill Video Games ETF (NERD), with the Invesco Next Gen Media and Gaming ETF (GGME) as a broader gaming and media fund.
